registry_rule: One entry per measure REPORTED as under consideration for the Autumn Budget on 28 October 2026. This is a pre-event scoreability registry, not a claims lane: it records what each measure would BE as a PolicyEngine-UK reform and whether the certified engine can express it, so that on Budget day a counterpart can be computed immediately rather than the work starting then. It stages NO value claims — the revenue figures in circulation are journalism citing third parties, and the #86 rule applies: a re-published figure belongs to its originator, not to the outlet. When HM Treasury and the OBR publish the scorecard and the EFO costings on the day, those become claims through the existing OBR/HMT lanes and join to these measure keys.
verification_note: Every pe_reform_delta path in this file was RESOLVED against an installed policyengine-uk 2.89.2 at authoring time, and the baseline values recorded below are what that engine returns for 2026 — not values copied from reporting. A measure whose path does not resolve is recorded not_expressible with the engine gap named, never guessed.

computability.expressible: every leg is a resolvable parameter in the certified engine
computability.partial: some legs resolve; the missing ones are named in `missing`
computability.not_expressible: the engine has no representation; `why` names the gap

measures.title: Align capital gains tax rates with income tax rates
measures.source_note: Widely reported as the leading broad-based option with the 'big three' ruled out; reported as previously supported by the Prime Minister, the Chancellor, the Chief Secretary and the Pensions Minister.
measures.behavioural_note: PE-UK carries a CGT behavioural response (capital_gains_behavioural_response, relative_capital_gains_mtr_change, elasticity at gov.simulation.capital_gains_responses.elasticity), so this measure can be scored BOTH static and post-behavioural. That matters more here than anywhere else in the registry: realisations respond strongly to the rate, published estimates disagree mostly about that response, and a static-only PE number would not be comparable to a behavioural OBR costing.

measures.title: Remove the capital gains uplift on death for inherited assets
measures.source_note: Reported as a possible measure raising £1.5-2bn annually.
measures.why: The certified engine models CGT on realised gains within the simulation year and has no representation of death, bequest or the base-cost uplift, so there is no parameter to move and no household event to attach the measure to. Scoring it needs an engine capability, not a registry entry.

measures.title: Reduce or remove the 25% tax-free pension lump sum
measures.source_note: Reported as a possible measure worth around £2bn a year; currently capped at £268,275.
measures.why: VERIFIED, not assumed: gov.hmrc.pensions has no tax-free lump sum parameter at the certified pin (probed and raised AttributeError). The engine carries pension CONTRIBUTIONS and their relief, plus a lump_sum_income input variable, but not the pension commencement lump sum or its cap. So the most-reported pensions measure of this Budget cannot be scored at all today.

measures.title: Extend National Insurance beyond employment income
measures.source_note: Reported at around £22bn annually, and 'deeply unpopular'.
measures.why: The NI base in the certified engine is employment and self-employment earnings; there is no parameter that widens the charge to investment, property or pension income. A counterpart would be a new charge, not a parameter change.

measures.title: Extend the personal allowance and threshold freeze
measures.source_note: Reported as the most politically charged option and the one touching the most people; the rates pledge does not cover thresholds.
measures.baseline_construction_note: A freeze is only measurable against an INDEXED counterfactual — the world where the thresholds had been uprated. That counterfactual is a registered baseline world question (#13), and it is exactly the axis #67 found undecomposed on the OBR's own PA/HRT freeze re-estimates. The registry does not pretend a freeze is a delta on current law.

measures.title: Annual wealth tax of 2% on net assets above £10m
measures.source_note: Reported as divisive with cabinet opposition; revenue estimates range from nil to £26bn, which is itself the finding — the spread is about behaviour and coverage, not arithmetic.
measures.caveat: Expressible does NOT mean credible: the engine applies the schedule to total_wealth from survey-imputed wealth, which is the weakest data in the certified world for exactly the population this measure targets. A PE number here should be published with that stated, or not published.

measures.title: Replace council tax and stamp duty with an annual land value tax
measures.source_note: Reported at around 1.3%; the Prime Minister is reported to have ruled out major property-tax change at the first Budget. Kept in the registry because it is the structural reform this administration is most associated with, and because a ruled-out measure is a scoreable counterfactual.
measures.missing: The abolition leg resolves, and land values exist (household_land_value, land_value), but there is no LVT RATE parameter to levy against them and no stamp-duty abolition switch. So PE can currently model the hole, not the replacement.

measures.title: High Value Council Tax Surcharge on English homes over £2m
measures.source_note: Announced at the November 2025 Budget, taking effect April 2028, £2,500-£7,500 by band. Already law, so it belongs in the certified world's baseline rather than in a Budget-day reform — recorded here so it is not double-counted as new.
measures.why: No surcharge parameter at the certified pin. Because it is already announced, the more important question is whether the certified world's 2028 baseline INCLUDES it; if not, every 2028 counterpart in the repo is measured against the wrong law.

measures.title: Higher income tax rates on property income from April 2027
measures.source_note: Reported as taking effect April 2027 regardless of this Budget.
measures.why: The engine taxes property income at the main income tax rates with no separate schedule, so a property-specific rate has no parameter. Same baseline-integrity question as the council tax surcharge: is the 2027 certified baseline already carrying it?

measures.title: Increase the surcharge on bank profits above £100m
measures.source_note: Reported as part of the business-levy package.
measures.why: Out of scope for a household microsimulation: the incidence falls on firms and the certified engine has no firm entity. Recorded rather than omitted so the registry states the whole reported package and its coverage honestly — roughly half of the reported Budget is not household-modellable at all, which is itself worth saying out loud.
